summary: Allowed E. M. LeBoiteaux to be hired at the Bureau of the Census for experimental work developing tabulating machinery, after a noncompetitive Civil Service Commission examination.
Repealed the November 15, 1905, executive order governing appointments to Isthmian Canal Commission positions on the Isthmus of Panama.
Amended the civil-service rules on which Isthmian Canal Commission positions are excepted from examination.
Withdrew lands in Minnesota, including an island in Aitkin Lake, from sale for the War Department's reservoir system at the headwaters of the Mississippi River.
Enlarged the Uintah Forest Reserve, adding lands in Utah and Wyoming and closing them to settlement, apart from valid existing entries.
Allowed Walter R. Brinckerhoff to be appointed chief of the leprosy hospital station in Hawaii, subject to a noncompetitive examination.
Expanded the Sevier Forest Reserve in Utah, first set apart in May 1905, and reserved the added lands from settlement.
Extended the boundaries of the Manti Forest Reserve in Utah, established in 1903, closing the added lands to settlement.
Temporarily withdrew public lands at Diamond Head, Kupikipikio Point and Punchbowl Hill in Hawaii for military use until surveys could fix permanent military reservations.

Ordered every executive department to form an advisory committee on printing to cut unnecessary matter, tables and illustrations from reports, and set rules keeping annual reports to concise accounts of work and spending.
Enlarged the Fish Lake Forest Reserve in Utah to take in additional lands partly covered with timber.
Allowed Mrs. Jeannette L. Cavanagh to be reinstated as a classified laborer in the Department of Agriculture, by an endorsement on a senator's letter.
Permitted William A. Barr to be reappointed in the Post-Office Department despite the civil-service rules' one-year limit.
Gave the U.S. Board on Geographic Names the job of fixing place names in the United States and its insular possessions, requiring officials to submit new names for approval before publication.
Created the Beaver Forest Reserve on public lands in Utah, reserving them from entry or settlement.
Set apart the La Sal Forest Reserve on timbered public lands in Utah and Colorado, closing them to entry or settlement.

Extended the 1902 order barring federal employees from lobbying Congress for pay raises or other legislation to cover workers in independent government establishments as well as executive departments.
Added mounted customs inspectors on the Mexican border to Schedule A, excepting them from civil-service examination.
Allowed Mary H. Donnelly to be reinstated as a clerk in the Office of the Chief of Ordnance without regard to the civil-service rules.
Authorized Charles S. Brown's appointment as an inspector in the Government Printing Office, subject to a noncompetitive examination.
Moved certain lands from the Bismarck land district in North Dakota to the Fargo land district.
Redrew the Fort Washakie Military Reservation in Wyoming to match a new survey, shifting one corner to leave out ground occupied by Indian school buildings.
Abolished the military reservation on Malagi (Malahi) Island in Laguna de Bay, Luzon, in the Philippine Islands.
Reserved Yes Lake, Yes Bay, Back Bay and strips of surrounding shore in Alaska as a salmon hatchery site, protecting Native rights to take fish and fuel there.
Let Charles H. Ingram, who had resigned from the Treasury Department in 1903, take a clerical job in the War Department without examination.
Gave the Spanish Treaty Claims Commission until September 2, 1906, to finish its work.
Set apart block 77 of the Randlett, Utah, town site for the Protestant Episcopal Church to use for missionary and cemetery purposes benefiting the Ute Indians.
Allowed Clayton G. Coleman to be reinstated as a special agent of the General Land Office despite the one-year limit in the civil-service rules.
Reserved Indian Key, a ninety-acre island in Tampa Bay, Florida, for the Department of Agriculture as a preserve and breeding ground for native birds.
Permitted William M. Geddes, longtime disbursing agent for government exhibits at expositions, to become a fourth-class clerk in the Treasury Department without meeting civil-service rules.
Allowed Joseph Fought to be promoted to clerk in the Treasury Department without regard to the civil-service rules.
Let John H. Smith be hired as a laborer in the Bureau of Engraving and Printing without following the regulations for appointing laborers.
Rewrote the 1905 order on pay for the Advisory Board of Engineers on Panama Canal plans: $5,000 each on completing the report, $15 a day while working, and travel costs.
Redrew the boundary between the Bismarck and Fargo land districts in North Dakota, moving certain lands along with their records and business.
Abolished the Mangum land district in Oklahoma and moved its lands, business and archives to the Lawton land district.
Established the Fruita Forest Reserve on public lands in Colorado and closed them to settlement.
Allowed nine men who had proved themselves in other posts to be appointed special agents of the Treasury Department without meeting civil-service rules.
Required laborers who do classified-grade work to be appointed through civil-service certification, and let such laborers already doing that work well be brought into the classified service.
Reserved public lands at Unalaklik, Alaska, for the Army Signal Corps to operate military cable and telegraph lines.
Set new salaries for the Isthmian Canal Commission, including $30,000 a year for Chairman Theodore P. Shonts and the chief engineer, plus housing and travel allowances.
Lowered U.S. duties on certain German goods, including crude tartar, brandies, still wines and artworks, in return for Germany granting American products its conventional tariff from March 1, 1906.
Let Mrs. Katherine Moynihan be appointed to a Post-Office Department position without examination.
Reinstated James T. Peterson and Clarence W. Allen at the Mobile, Alabama, post office, after the department found they had been unjustly removed.

Put a committee's tuberculosis-prevention rules into force across federal offices and workshops, requiring posted rules, examinations of employees suspected of having the disease, and sanitary inspections of public buildings.
Rewrote a consular regulation so consuls certify invoices for U.S.-bound goods sent by mail or messenger, without requiring shippers to appear in person.
Rewrote a consular regulation directing consuls to check each invoice item, consult chambers of commerce, and, when needed, demand bills of sale, samples or inspection of whole shipments.
Allowed Robert Lee Gray to be appointed assistant messenger in the Department of Justice without examination.
Permitted Mrs. Coila B. Ashby to be reinstated as a clerk in the Interior Department despite the reinstatement rule's one-year limit.
Reshaped the Fort Egbert Military Reservation in Alaska, adding public lands and handing a no-longer-useful portion to the Interior Department for disposal.
Enlarged the Gallatin Forest Reserve in Montana and reserved the added lands from settlement.
Waived the citizenship requirement so J. F. Moreno, a British subject with twelve years in the diplomatic and consular services, could take a civil-service examination.
Created the North Platte Forest Reserve on public lands in Nebraska, closing them to entry and settlement.
Reserved public lands on Batan Island and Cacraray Island in the Philippines for military purposes, including the western part of Batan, about 25 square miles.
Created the Blue Mountains Forest Reserve in Oregon, absorbing most of the Baker City Forest Reserve, which it replaced; lands left out were restored to the public domain.
Reserved certain lands in Alaska for an agricultural experiment station.
Clarified that the Isthmian Canal Commission chairman, the Canal Zone governor and the chief engineer are paid actual expenses while traveling on commission business, effective February 26, 1906.
Set aside the Middle Islands at Rock Harbor, Michigan, for lighthouse purposes.
Gave up the Grass Island military reservation in Grays Harbor, Washington, placing the island under the Interior Department since it was not needed for defense.
Redefined the boundaries of the Billings land district in Montana.
Waived the citizenship rule so Pyeng E. Yoon, a Korean subject, could be a Korean-speaking clerk in the Honolulu post office after an examination found no eligible candidates.
Let Charles P. Galpin be appointed a classified laborer in the Bureau of Pensions without examination.
Allowed Joseph F. Laporte to be reinstated in the post-office service despite the time limit on reinstatement.
Let Jacob S. McClure, a Civil War veteran whose laborer job at the Topeka pension agency was abolished, be reemployed in a classified position.
Allowed Benjamin B. Cox to be reinstated at the Mobile, Alabama, post office without regard to civil-service Rule IX.
Set apart the Helena Forest Reserve on public lands in Montana, closing them to entry and settlement.
Reserved two sections of land in Mississippi, 307.54 acres in all, as a target range for the Revenue-Cutter Service.
Allowed Harry H. Brewster to move from the unclassified South St. Joseph post office to finance clerk at the St. Joseph, Missouri, post office without meeting civil-service requirements.
Permitted Mrs. Mary A. McDonald to be appointed a clerk in the Department of the Interior without examination.
Enlarged the Ashland Forest Reserve in Oregon, first established in 1893, and reserved the added lands from settlement.
Established the Vernon Forest Reserve on public lands in Utah.
Abolished the office of Surveyor General for Florida.
Temporarily moved the San Francisco land office to Oakland, California, after the building that housed it was destroyed.
Allowed George M. Shafer, a Civil War veteran, to be permanently appointed a watchman in the Department of the Interior without meeting civil-service requirements.
Created the Ruby Mountains Forest Reserve on public lands in Nevada.
Enlarged the Weiser Forest Reserve in Idaho, established in May 1905, and closed the added lands to settlement.
Reserved certain lands in Juneau, Alaska, for educational purposes.
Revoked the November 1905 order abolishing the Bent land district in Colorado, keeping the district and its office at Lamar.
Designated Maj. Gen. F. C. Ainsworth and Brig. Gen. J. Franklin Bell, in that order, to act as Secretary of War during the Secretary's absence.
Set apart the Fillmore Forest Reserve on public lands in Utah.
Allowed Harry E. Burns, honorably discharged as a Navy fireman, to be appointed fireman in any department at Washington.

Transferred historical archives from the State Department to the Library of Congress, including Revolutionary-era orderly books, Albert Gallatin's Treasury correspondence, Burr Conspiracy papers and Jefferson Davis papers.
Opened the ceded, unallotted lands of the Crow Indian Reservation in Montana to settlement and entry under the homestead, town-site and mineral land laws.
Allowed O. Louis Cleven to be appointed in the Bureau of the Census for experimental work on tabulating machinery, subject to a noncompetitive examination.
Invited state and territorial governors to send militia, at their own expense, to the Jamestown tercentennial celebration on Hampton Roads, Virginia.
Created the Bear River Forest Reserve on public lands in Idaho and Utah, in place of the Logan Forest Reserve.
Enlarged the Wichita Forest Reserve in Oklahoma Territory, established in 1901, and reserved the added lands from settlement.
Trimmed the Uinta Forest Reserve, releasing certain lands in Utah and Wyoming and opening them to settlement, with entry allowed after ninety days' notice.
Allowed Mrs. M. C. Kratz to be reinstated in the Treasury Department, since she had been removed through inadvertence.
Exempted clerical jobs on the Isthmus of Panama paying under $75 a month from civil-service examination and eased transfers and promotions among classified positions there.
Enlarged the Hell Gate Forest Reserve in Montana, created in October 1905, closing the added lands to settlement.
Opened the unallotted lands ceded by the Shoshone and Arapahoe tribes on the Shoshone or Wind River Reservation in Wyoming to settlement under the homestead, townsite, coal and mineral land laws.

Dealt with gilsonite, asphaltum and elaterite lands in the former Uncompahgre Indian Reservation in Utah, upholding mining claims recorded before 1891 and providing for sale of the remaining mineral lands.
Allowed Jesse F. Gates, severely wounded in the Spanish war, to be reinstated as a classified laborer in the Treasury Department.
Transferred the "Government Acre" in Oklahoma from the Interior Department to the Treasury Department for a post office and other government purposes.
Reserved certain lands inside the Salt Lake Forest Reserve in Utah as a nursery site.
